PHIL 25601.description: Examines AI through philosophical history, knowledge, ethics, justice and policy, including implications for labor, equity and the environment.

PHIL 30000.description: Examines philosophical questions about computation, intelligence and machine minds; evaluates AI capabilities and limitations.

PHIL 31400.description: Develops philosophical arguments about the ethical, social and political responsibilities and risks of AI.

PHIL 32300.description: Uses computing to investigate philosophical questions, including code-based demonstrations, modeling philosophical ideas and ethical reflection.

PHIL 41400.description: Analyzes advanced philosophical questions about machine learning and AI through argument, writing and evaluation of emerging proposals.

CS 17600.description: Develops Python programming with loops, functions and data structures, then uses Pandas and Matplotlib for data cleaning, transformation and visualization.

CS 18000.description: Develops algorithmic problem solving and object-oriented programming, including debugging, searching, sorting, files, interfaces and abstract data types.

CS 18200.description: Teaches discrete mathematical reasoning for computing: proofs, sets, relations, counting, graphs, recursion, logic, automata and computability.

CS 24300.description: Implements learning and reasoning systems in Python, including knowledge representation, model training and validation, regressors, classifiers, constraint reasoning and search.

CS 36100.description: Analyzes professional ethics and the societal impact of computing, including algorithmic bias, data ethics, privacy and legal issues.

MA 16010.description: Develops differential and integral calculus with optimization, numerical integration and applications to life, management and social sciences.

MA 16020.description: Develops integration methods, infinite series, multivariable differentiation and integration, optimization and differential equations.

MA 16100.description: Introduces single-variable differential and integral calculus and its applications.

MA 16500.description: Introduces single-variable differential and integral calculus, applications and conic sections.

PHIL 20700.description: Applies ethical frameworks to professional engineering, technology and design cases in global and cultural contexts.

PHIL 20800.description: Develops professional ethical reasoning and case analysis for data science.

PHIL 30100.description: Surveys ancient Greek philosophy from early schools through Plato and Aristotle.

PHIL 30200.description: Surveys medieval philosophical traditions, emphasizing metaphysics, knowledge and ethics.

PHIL 30300.description: Studies philosophical thinkers from the Renaissance to the early nineteenth century and interprets their work in historical context.

PHIL 30400.description: Studies major movements and thinkers in nineteenth-century philosophy.

PHIL 30600.description: Critically examines twentieth-century philosophical traditions and selected major thinkers.

PHIL 31000.description: Interprets classical Chinese philosophers and evaluates their arguments about morality, human nature, ritual and government.

PHIL 22100.description: Examines philosophical accounts of scientific method, discovery, explanation, revolutions and values in scientific change.

PHIL 32200.description: Examines the nature, history and human implications of technology through philosophical texts and criticism.

PHIL 35000.description: Introduces mathematical probability together with philosophical problems of induction and scientific reasoning.

PHIL 42100.description: Examines philosophical accounts of explanation, confirmation, reduction, laws and the foundations of scientific theories.

PHIL 55300.description: Develops mathematical logic, formal languages, metatheory and precise abstract arguments about mathematical foundations.

AD 22000.description: Uses computer graphics and digital imagery for creative expression and fine-art projects.

AD 26700.description: Creates and enhances photographic imagery using digital imaging software and artistic critique.

AD 32600.description: Creates interactive audiovisual artworks using electronics, microcontrollers, coding and interfaces responding to physical events.

ANTH 21000.description: Examines the social origins, politics, identities and cultural consequences of technologies through anthropology.

COM 25100.description: Develops information literacy while analyzing how media and communication technologies affect people, institutions and society.

COM 41500.description: Develops speech communication, group discussion and presentation skills for technical problems.

ENGL 22300.description: Uses literature and criticism to examine technological innovation, creativity and new media.

ENGL 32001.description: Uses rhetorical theory to evaluate generative AI and to create and critique writing and workplace documents with attention to ethical use.

ENGL 42100.description: Develops rhetorical approaches to technical documents, research, usability and accessibility.

ENGL 42400.description: Develops professional writing and documentation for technical industries and non-specialist audiences.

HIST 28400.description: Examines the historical, political and economic development of computing and its changing social uses.

HIST 30701.description: Examines the history of automating cognition and its relationships with philosophical theories, social power and ethical debates.

HIST 30705.description: Traces the history of data collection, privacy, state power and computing, including contemporary ethical implications of algorithms.

HIST 38506.description: Analyzes U.S. computing and quantification history in relation to social problems, democracy, power and justice.

POL 22800.description: Analyzes policymaking and the ethical, legal and social governance of data science and AI.

POL 25801.description: Examines emerging technologies in international affairs and strategies for governance, foreign policy and diplomacy.

SOC 34400.description: Analyzes how social and cultural forces shape environmental problems and support for solutions.

SOC 38100.description: Analyzes social changes, inequalities, control and resistance associated with data and AI technologies.

PHIL 41500.description: Applies philosophical reasoning, argument, textual analysis and communication to internships, research or professional experience; objectives vary by placement.

area-c-d-level.summary: At least 6 credits across Areas C and D must be at the 30000+ level. The later course note specifies the 30000–50000 level; retain both source formulations.

cla-core.summary: Published CLA core range: 35–76 credits. Complete the applicable diversity and foundational requirements; overlap is allowed outside the major. Degree + students with a second major outside CLA are exempt from the CLA core.

cla-disciplines.summary: Take one course in each of six different CLA disciplines, distinguished by prefix; undistributed credit does not satisfy this rule. Published range: 6–18 credits. Accreditation-based exemptions are conditional.

cla-social.summary: Complete one course from the linked Social Diversity Selective List; published range: 1–3 credits. The approved list is not yet extracted here.

cla-language.summary: Complete 10100, 10200, 20100 and 20200 OR 10500 and 20500 in one world language; published range: 8–16 credits. Exact eligible language/proficiency details require advising; no generic codes are invented.

cla-foundational.summary: Meet AI working competency, humanities, behavioral/social science, information literacy, two science requirements, science/technology/society, written communication, oral communication and quantitative reasoning with approved coursework. Published range: 21–36 credits; courses can overlap CLA diversity requirements. The approved university pools are not extracted for this BA.

cla-overlap-exemptions.summary: Double counting is allowed across the plan except within major requirements. Programs whose accreditation is threatened by CLA Core I/II can be exempt from those categories but still require Core III. Degree + students with a second major outside CLA are exempt from the CLA core; applicability is conditional.

electives.summary: Published general elective range: 0–34 credits. This is not an additional fixed load or a named required course pool.

gpa.summary: Maintain a 2.0 GPA in courses applying toward the PHIL major, with no P/NP fulfillment, and a 2.0 graduation GPA for the BA.

major-notes.summary: PHIL 15000 cannot count toward the major. Courses used for Areas A, B or C cannot count for Area D. At least 6 credits in Areas C and D must be at the 30000–50000 level.

pass-no-pass.summary: P/NP cannot fulfill CLA core, major, minor or certificate requirements.

university-core.summary: Meet all ten listed university foundational outcomes, including AI working competency and two science requirements. The Senate maintains approved selectives; these obligations overlap the CLA foundational list and are not counted twice.

civics.summary: The catalog directs all baccalaureate students to complete 12 Civics Literacy podcasts and episode quizzes, then the knowledge test. The requirement bears no financial costs and does not affect GPA; do not invent a credit-bearing course.

residence.summary: Complete resident study at Purdue for at least two semesters and at least 32 approved semester hours required for the degree, expected to be junior level (30000+) or above. These may overlap major coursework.

prerequisite-information.summary: The catalog directs prerequisite checks to authenticated myPurdue. Current prerequisites remain unverified; missing values do not mean no prerequisites.

world-language-notes.summary: The catalog lists offered languages but states that acceptable languages and required proficiency vary by program and require advising. No language offering is inferred to be a fixed BA course.

_outcomes.text: Identify central AI concepts and algorithms.
Explain principles of machine learning, neural networks and other AI techniques.
Summarize AI ethics and societal impacts.
Evaluate strengths and limitations of AI approaches.
Develop reasoned critiques of AI research papers and projects.
